analyst_view.overall: Early view: Gladbach are bottom with four points under Alexander Blessin after a 3-1 loss at Hamburg, where Ko Itakura was sent off with the score 1-1. Frankfurt under Adi Hütter drew 2-2 at Paderborn with ten men after Elias Baum's second yellow. Both bans are for one match and are served on 21 November, so Itakura and Baum should be free to play here. One injury list has Tim Kleindienst out until late November.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals. Gladbach concede easily and Frankfurt's games have been open, but a struggling home side may play more carefully, and Kleindienst's fitness is uncertain. I keep it where the site has it.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Nothing I found suggests either side will change how they play, so I stay with the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. I lean higher: Gladbach are in a relegation fight and both teams had a man sent off in their last match, so the game could be tense and physical.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.1 shots. Both teams should get chances against weak defending, which the model already expects.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.1 shots on target. Jonathan Burkardt is scoring for Frankfurt and Gladbach let in three at Hamburg, which fits the high figure. I see no reason to move it this early.
